author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Input-validation boundary: the user-controlled `page` request parameter is bound as a primitive `int` (Spring rejects non-numeric input at binding), then clamped at the boundary with `Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE)` before any downstream use. Both consumers (`findPaginatedForOwnersLastName` and `addPaginationModel`) receive the clamped `currentPage`; the raw `page` is no longer used past line 102, so no unclamped path survives. `Math.max` is total over int, so `Integer.MIN_VALUE` clamps to 1 with no underflow at the later `page - 1`.

Data access: pagination reaches the database only via `PageRequest.of(currentPage - 1, 5)` through the derived repository query `findByLastNameStartingWith`. No string-concatenated query text and no request-derived value in query structure, satisfying the injection-into-data-access control in docs/security-principles.md.

Output escaping and template injection: `currentPage` enters the model as an int and is rendered by Thymeleaf, including the expression-preprocessing constructs `__${currentPage - 1}__` and `__${currentPage + 1}__` in owners/ownersList.html. An int can carry no expression syntax, and the clamp strictly narrows the range now reaching those constructs (previously 0 and negatives could reach them), so the change moves this path in the safe direction rather than widening it.

No new attack surface: no endpoint added, no mapping or HTTP method changed, no management-endpoint exposure altered, no change to `setAllowedFields` mass-assignment disallow list, no file/resource path composed from request input, no deserialization, no error message carrying internal detail outward.

Secret hygiene: swept the full change set for credential-shaped identifiers (password, secret, token, apikey, api_key, credential, passwd, key) with a fixed-string case-insensitive search - zero hits. No new credential of any kind is introduced.

Supply chain: the change set is exactly two files (OwnerController.java, OwnerControllerTests.java) per scripts/changeset.sh --name-only. No build.gradle, no dependency declaration, no repository or version change, so no new artifact enters the resolution graph and the existing dependency posture is untouched. The pre-existing test-scope Mockito/AssertJ imports added in the test file are already project dependencies.

Test change is test-scope only (MockMvc-driven controller test asserting HTTP 200, view name, model `currentPage`, and a captured `Pageable` page number of 0 for both `0` and `-1`); it adds no production surface and no security-relevant configuration.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The new test iterates a `for (String pageBelowFirst : List.of("0", "-1"))` loop over two request cases, calling mockMvc.perform/andExpect inside the loop body. testing-principles.md's Assertions section bars branching/loops in test bodies ("No branching in assertions | No if/else, switch, or loops") and the Agent Decision Checklist item 4 ("Linearity: No branching or loops in the test body?") applies equally to a hand-rolled loop over request scenarios.
findings.fix: Replace the for loop with @ParameterizedTest(name="page={0}") @ValueSource(strings = {"0", "-1"}) void theOwnerListingShouldShowFirstPageWhenPageIsBelowFirst(String pageBelowFirst), moving the single mockMvc.perform/andExpect chain and the verify/captor assertions into the parameterized method body.

findings.description: testing-principles.md § Test Naming states the BDD school (`the{Subject}Should{Outcome}`) applies to tests written or modified from 2026-07-31 onward; this test is newly added (today, 2026-08-07) and is named after the production method (`processFindForm...`), which the brief calls out by name as the anti-pattern to avoid ("not processFindFormByLastName"). The name should state the outcome, not the handler method.

`.andExpect(model().attribute("currentPage", 1))` uses a bare literal `1` for the expected first-page number. testing-principles.md § Three-Tier Data Naming calls this a Tier-1 meaningful value that should carry a role-describing name (mirroring the production FIRST_PAGE constant), not a mystery literal.
findings.fix: Introduce a small private static final int FIRST_PAGE = 1 (or reuse an existing test constant) and reference it in the assertion instead of the bare 1.

approved_aspects: The fix's core behavior is verified from two independent angles: the rendered model's currentPage attribute and the Pageable actually sent to the repository (getPageNumber() == 0), which is a stronger check than asserting the HTTP status alone.
Test correctly covers both page=0 and page=-1, matching the bug description ("any page below 1"), not just the single reported case.
./gradlew test passes with the new test included; no regression in the existing suite.
